**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off

**Issue:** `os.environ.get("SMTP_PASSWORD", "smtp-prod-backup-77")` embeds a production credential as a default. If `SMTP_PASSWORD` is unset (the cron case the comment describes), every runner authenticates with this shared secret. The value is also permanent git history once merged, so repo readers can reuse it against `smtp.internal.example`.

**Fix:** Require the env var and fail (or no-op with an error log) when it is missing; mount the secret into the cron job. Rotate this password if it was ever real.

```suggestion
        s.login("notifications", os.environ["SMTP_PASSWORD"])
```

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change embeds a production SMTP credential in source as a default fallback.

## Why this is blocking

`mailer.py` replaces the required `SMTP_PASSWORD` env lookup with:

```python
os.environ.get("SMTP_PASSWORD", "smtp-prod-backup-77")
```

That default is a real-looking shared secret checked into the repo. Anyone with read access to the code (or the git history after merge) can authenticate as `notifications` against `smtp.internal.example`. The comment makes the intent explicit: keep mail working when the secret is not mounted, which means the fallback is meant for production-shaped environments.

## What to do instead

Fail fast when `SMTP_PASSWORD` is missing (or skip send with a clear log), and mount the secret into the cron environment the same way other jobs get credentials. Rotate `smtp-prod-backup-77` immediately if it was ever a live password — it is now exposed in this branch even if the PR is closed.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
